updates.headline: Wetlands Authority files status report on the proposed interim zone; no order reported
updates.summary: The Member Secretary of the Tamil Nadu State Wetlands Authority filed a status report before the Madras High Court setting out a revised interim Zone of Influence of about 316.76 acres (128.19 ha) across 36 survey numbers, prepared after 23 representations from landowners, developers and others. The report proposes that construction inside the zone be regulated according to site-specific scientific and hydrological conditions rather than banned outright, with a No Objection Certificate from the District Level Wetlands Management Committee, and lists safeguards: no blocking or diverting of drains and inlet/outlet channels, no dumping of waste or debris in drainage paths, restrictions on discharging untreated sewage or effluent into connected watercourses, no permanent alteration of hydrological connections and no Red Category industries.
updates.changed: The State's proposal is now on record as a written status report, with listed safeguards and a stated NOC route.
updates.not_changed: No order adopting the proposal has been reported. The report itself describes the zone as interim, not the final boundary.

updates.headline: PMK leader questions the reduced protection zone and calls for wetland boundaries to be notified
updates.summary: PMK leader Anbumani Ramadoss accused the Wetlands Authority of favouring private developers after it told the High Court that, following consultations on 30 September, the zone would be cut to about 316 acres. He described the earlier zone as 8,397 acres. He called for scientifically determined zones with construction regulated rather than banned outright, full survey and notification of wetland boundaries as directed by the Supreme Court on 11 December 2024, and abandonment of the wall and walkway works along the marsh.
updates.changed: Political opposition to the reduced zone is now on record.
updates.not_changed: A political statement has no legal effect on the court proceedings or on approvals.

updates.headline: Wetlands Authority tells High Court the interim zone can be limited to 36 survey numbers (128.19 ha)
updates.summary: The Tamil Nadu State Wetlands Authority told the Madras High Court that 36 survey numbers covering about 128.19 hectares could serve as the interim Zone of Influence, and that private patta lands had been excluded from this proposal. Counsel for CREDAI Chennai said the proposal was acceptable to the developers' body. The court directed a report to be filed by 14 October and said it would consider orders after reading it.
updates.changed: The State's proposed interim zone is far smaller than the 1 km zone reportedly used for the current approval pause.
updates.not_changed: This is a submission, not a court order. Exclusion of patta land from the proposal does not by itself make any parcel unrestricted, and land outside the 36 survey numbers is not automatically cleared for construction.

updates.headline: PMK demands the 3 km wall and walkway works on the marsh be stopped
updates.summary: Anbumani Ramadoss demanded that the State stop and remove a roughly 3 km retaining wall and pathway being built on the marshland under the Neithal Recovery Mission, which the State is funding with a World Bank loan (₹21.5 crore allocated to the Pallikaranai works), saying it could obstruct rainwater flow and raise flood risk for nearby homes. He warned of a protest if the works continue.
updates.changed: The wall works have become a public point of contention.
updates.not_changed: No order stopping the works has been reported. The works are separate from the Zone of Influence case.

updates.headline: Officials meet to revise the proposed interim Zone of Influence
updates.summary: Officials met on 30 September to review the proposed boundary, following the court's directions; the reduced proposal presented in court on 12 October followed. One secondary source adds that the review considered satellite imagery, water spread, drainage paths, low-lying land, infrastructure and links to nearby wetlands.
updates.changed: The State's working proposal was revised downward.
updates.not_changed: An internal meeting outcome is not a notification or an order. Minutes of the meeting have not been seen.

updates.headline: MLA raises flood concerns over concrete wall and walkway around the marsh
updates.summary: PMK MLA Sowmiya Anbumani inspected the 3 km concrete compound wall and walkway being built around the marshland under the ₹21 crore Neithal restoration and protection works, and said it could block natural rainwater flow and cause stagnation in nearby residential areas. updates.changed: First public objection in this period to the wall works.
updates.not_changed: No government response or order was reported.

updates.headline: Wetlands Authority files NCSCM interim Zone of Influence map; says construction can be regulated, not banned
updates.summary: The Tamil Nadu State Wetlands Authority told the Madras High Court that construction in the Zone of Influence could be regulated rather than banned, and placed on record an interim map prepared by the National Centre for Sustainable Coastal Management. The map proposes a variable width instead of a uniform 1 km — zero metres along about 30 km of the 77.85 km boundary studied, and more than 100 m along roughly a third of it. The court took the map on record and gave CREDAI and other parties time to respond, listing the matter for 7 September.
updates.changed: The State's position shifted from a uniform 1 km buffer towards a science-based, variable-width zone.
updates.not_changed: This was a submission. No order lifting the approval restriction was reported.

background.headline: NGT (Southern Zone) judgment: no approvals that may alter the marsh until the Integrated Management Plan is ready
background.summary: In O.A. No. 91 of 2023 (SZ), the tribunal directed that, until the Integrated Management Plan is completed, the authorities should not grant approvals or permissions that may alter the character of the marshland, and that CMDA may grant approvals in the marshland and its zone of influence only after the plan is prepared on the basis of the Wetlands Authority's survey (paras 44–46). The judgment refers to a general 1 km zone of influence recommended in a draft management plan and records the Wetlands Authority's position that the zone is site-specific; it sets no deadline, directing the agencies to expedite the plan.

current_status.text: No order lifting the approval restriction around the Pallikaranai Ramsar site has been reported. CMDA's October 2025 office order pausing approvals in the Ramsar site and a 1 km zone is described from reports (official copy not yet reviewed). The State's proposed interim Zone of Influence (128.19 ha, 36 survey numbers) is a proposal before the Madras High Court, not an order.
